claims.text: Al0.7CoCrFeNi has an initial dual-phase FCC/B2 lamellar microstructure.
The initial Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy is strong but brittle.
The brittleness of the initial alloy is caused by stress concentration at incoherent FCC/B2 interfaces.
Treatment at approximately 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours in a hexahedron-anvil apparatus will transform the alloy's lamellar topology.
The HPHT-induced topology will be a hierarchically patterned FCC/B2 microstructure.
The transformed FCC/B2 interfaces will be coherent.
Coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation transfer between the FCC and B2 phases.
Dislocation transfer across coherent interfaces alleviates interfacial stress concentrations.
The hierarchical coherent microstructure enables stacking-fault formation and twinning in addition to dislocation transfer.
The enabled deformation mechanisms promote homogeneous strain distribution.
Homogeneous strain distribution arrests interfacial cracking.
The HPHT-treated alloy will exhibit significantly improved ductility without sacrificing strength.
The fracture morphology will shift from isolated microcracks in the baseline to elongated cracks after HPHT treatment.
At high strain, the GND densities of the FCC and B2 phases will converge in the treated alloy.
There is a pressure-temperature window that can form coherent interfaces without causing phase decomposition or instability.
Conventional thermomechanical treatments will not produce the same hierarchical coherent microstructure or GND homogenization as HPHT treatment.
The degree of FCC/B2 GND-density convergence may depend on deformation strain rate and temperature.

contradictions.description: The initial material is described as homogenized, whereas the baseline is described as as-cast, without clarifying whether these are the same reference state or distinct samples.
